land.text: Persis, ruled by local Fratarakas 'subject to the' Seleucids from the end of the 3rd or the start of the 2nd century BC

predecessors.note: The Fratarakas page: the Fratarakas 'would have been subordinate to the Seleucids'; their rule is dated from c. 295 or c. 280 BC (disputed). This dossier starts at the independence the same page gives as 'circa 150 BC'; the earlier Frataraka decades are Seleucid land in the seleucid-empire dossier.

land.text: Persis, 'Incorporated into the Sasanian Empire in AD 224'; the kings' last, Ardashir V, is Ardashir I

successors.note: The Kings of Persis page: 'Succeeded by Pars (Sasanian province)'.

capitals.name: Istakhr (Estakhr, by Persepolis)
capitals.note: The Kings of Persis infobox gives Istakhr. The Fratarakas page disagrees about the earlier seat: traditionally Persepolis (an 'Istakhr (Persepolis)' mint), while Kritt argues the Frataraka coinage was struck at Susa. Coordinates are the gazetteer's Istakhr.

correction.text: Persis (Fars), the region the Fratarakas governed: 'Persis (Fārs), the region the Fratarakas governed' (Fratarakas page); the Kings of Persis 'ruled Persis (Pars) in southwestern Iran' (Kings of Persis page)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe; Cliopatria has no row for Persis (its Sasanian row begins in 215). Neither page gives an area or a boundary, so the gazetteer's Persis (about 157,000 km2) is the reading. The land does not change between -150 and 224 on either page: independence c. 150 BC, Parthian suzerainty from about 138 BC (kings keep their coinage, 'mlk'), Ardashir's wider conquests after 211/2 belong to the sasanian-empire dossier.

region.text: Persis (Pars, Fars) in southwestern Iran, the land of the Fratarakas and the Kings of Persis

ledger.note: c. 150 BC: Persis wins independence from the Seleucids under its frataraka Vahbarz (Wadfradad I). Fratarakas page: he 'obtained independence circa 150 BC' as Seleucid power waned; the Kings of Persis page has Strabo calling the early kings tributaries until c. 140 BC. The year is the page's 'circa'; the land is the region the Fratarakas governed.

region.text: Persis (Pars, Fars) in southwestern Iran, the land of the Fratarakas and the Kings of Persis

ledger.note: c. 138 BC: Persis becomes a vassal of the Parthian Empire under Mithridates I. Kings of Persis page: 'Later the frataraka Wadfradad II (fl. 138 BC) was made a vassal of the Iranian Parthian (Arsacid) Empire'; Strabo, quoted on the same page: 'the early kings of Persis were tributaries to the Seleucid rulers, until c.140 BC, when the Parthians conquered the region'; infobox status 'Vassal of the Parthian Empire'. The year is the page's 'fl. 138 BC' (Wadfradad II); no page gives a day or a treaty, and the region is the whole of Persis because the kings kept their own land and coinage. Mirrors parthian-empire /ledger/15 (vassal_start persis, which has -135; the pages here say c. 140/138 BC). [Added after review me-06-x, 2026-10-19; Kings of Persis page re-read the same day]

After 132 BC: the Kings of Persis replace the Fratarakas, 'most likely at the accession of Parthian king Phraates II (r. 132-127 BC)'. Same state and land; the coin table of the page shows drachms with Aramaic legends using the title 'mlk' (king). The page says 'after 132 BCE', not a year, so the year is the first of the span. The Parthian overlordship that began under Mithridates I (see wars) continues; the parthian-empire dossier records the vassal tint.

205/6: Pabag overthrows the Bazrangid king Gochihr and takes Istakhr, the house that becomes the Sasanians. Kings of Persis page: 'In 205/6, the local ruler Pabag overthrew the Bazrangid ruler Gochihr and took Istakhr.' He dies between 207 and 210 and is succeeded by his son Shapur (d. 211/2), then Ardashir V.

region.text: Persis (Pars, Fars) in southwestern Iran, the land of the Fratarakas and the Kings of Persis

ledger.note: 28 April 224: the vassalage ends when Ardashir (Ardashir V of Persis, 211/2-224) defeats Artabanus IV at Hormozdgan. Kings of Persis page: the kings 'ruled as vassal kings of the Parthian Empire, until they toppled them and established the Sasanian Empire'; infobox 'Incorporated into the Sasanian Empire: AD 224'. The Ardashir I page dates no earlier break (it says Artabanus declared Papak and Ardashir outlaws, undated, and that Ardashir began taking neighbouring lands 'in about 220'), so the vassal_end is set with the dissolve at 224, not at 215 as parthian-empire /ledger/65 has it (see notes). [Added after review me-06-x, 2026-10-19]

region.text: Persis (Pars, Fars) in southwestern Iran, the land of the Fratarakas and the Kings of Persis

ledger.note: 28 April 224: Ardashir defeats Artabanus IV on the Hormozdgan plain and the kingdom of Persis becomes the core of the Sasanian Empire. Kings of Persis infobox: 'Incorporated into the Sasanian Empire in AD 224'; Ardashir 'conquered the rest of Iran, establishing the Sasanian Empire in 224 as Ardashir I'. The month is from the Ardashir I page ('on April 28, 224, Ardashir faced the army of Artabanus IV in the Hormozdgan plain'). His conquests of Kerman, Isfahan, Susa and Characene are in the sasanian-empire dossier.

wars.name: Parthian conquest of Persis

zones.text: Persis (Pars, Fars) in southwestern Iran, the land of the Fratarakas and the Kings of Persis

wars.outcome: Mithridates I took control of Persis but let the local rulers stay: he installed Wadfradad II as frataraka with more autonomy and made Persis a Parthian vassal.
wars.note: The Mithridates I page gives no year for the Persis conquest, placing it 'around the same period' as the Demetrius II episode it dates to 138 BC; the Kings of Persis page has Wadfradad II 'fl. 138 BC'. The year -138 is therefore the page's context date, not a dated conquest. The parthian-empire dossier bridges it at -135.

wars.name: Ardashir's revolt against the Arsacids
wars.outcome: Ardashir, king of Persis from 211/2, subdued the neighbouring lands in defiance of Arsacid rule and on 28 April 224 defeated and killed Artabanus IV at Hormozdgan, founding the Sasanian Empire.
wars.note: Parthian Empire page: Ardashir I 'began subjugating the surrounding territories in defiance of Arsacid rule' (undated) and 'confronted Artabanus IV at the Battle of Hormozdgan on 28 April 224 AD'. Zones are left empty because the Persis land itself did not change hands; the conquered neighbours are recorded in the parthian-empire and sasanian-empire dossiers.

certainty.note: Neither page gives a boundary or an area; Persis is drawn as the region the sources name, with soft edges throughout.

notes:
State Cliopatria lacks (new_slug persis). Persis was listed as a needed dossier by the me-06-a (Parthian Empire) and me-06-c (Sasanian Empire) reports. One dossier covers the Fratarakas and the Kings of Persis (a dynasty change inside one state, master plan rule 2); it starts at the c. 150 BC independence, the earlier Frataraka decades (c. 280/295 BC on) being Seleucid land.

OVERLAP TO SETTLE: the pages end the kingdom in 224 ('Incorporated into the Sasanian Empire in AD 224'; Ardashir V reigns 211/2-224), but the sasanian-empire dossier (following Cliopatria's row, which starts in 215) already treats the Persis land as Sasanian from 215 (its found event with counterpart persis; the parthian-empire dossier ends its Persis vassal tint in 215 as well). Drawn together, the Fars land is claimed twice in 215-224. Suggested rule for the renderer: from 215 the sasanian-empire dossier wins on the overlapping cells, or truncate persis at 214. This dossier keeps 224 because that is what the pages say.

Parthian vassalage: the parthian-empire dossier carries vassal_start persis at -135 and vassal_end at 215. The pages here date the subjugation to about 138 BC (Mithridates I) and the kings' vassal status 'continued under later kings' until 224.

No rulers strip: the Kings of Persis page dates its kings by half-century only, except Vahshir II (c. 206-210), Pabag (took Istakhr 205/6) and Ardashir V (211/2-224).

Gazetteer: region Persis resolves (157,000 km2); no unknown names.

REPAIR 2026-10-19 (author, after review me-06-x): (1) Added vassal_start at -138 and vassal_end at 224 (April), counterpart parthian-empire, confidence 2 (the reviewer's blocking finding). Pages re-read: Kings of Persis ('Later the frataraka Wadfradad II (fl. 138 BC) was made a vassal of the Iranian Parthian (Arsacid) Empire'; 'ruled as vassal kings of the Parthian Empire, until they toppled them'; Strabo: tributaries of the Seleucids 'until c.140 BC, when the Parthians conquered the region'). ROUTE TO parthian-empire (me-06-a): move vassal_start persis from -135 to -138 and vassal_end persis from 215 to 224. (2) 215-224 OVERLAP, thin item: the Ardashir I page was re-read and gives no 215 for Persis. It has Ardashir crowned a local shah in 211/212 ('King of Persis - Reign: 211/2-224'), replacing his brother Shapur 'in 220' on one account, 'probably in about 220' beginning to take 'far and close lands', and Artabanus IV fighting him only on 28 April 224. The page therefore does not support 215 as the year Persis became Sasanian; 215 is Cliopatria's. I keep 224. ROUTE TO sasanian-empire (me-06-c): /ledger/0 (found, counterpart persis, 215) should be dated no earlier than the 211/2-224 span of Ardashir's kingship; the orchestrator must settle whether the renderer draws Fars as Persis (vassal tint) or Sasanian between 215 and 224, as 211 cells (about 53,000 km2) lie in both. I disagree with ending Persis at 214/215 because no page does. (3) Thin item, the Fratarakas' own seat for -150 to -132: the Fratarakas page was re-read and names no capital; it cites Kritt's view that the coinage 'was issued in Susa, rather than Persepolis as traditionally held' and lists an 'Istakhr (Persepolis) mint'. The capital entry therefore stays one entry (Istakhr by Persepolis) with the Susa alternative in its note; the page does not settle it. UPDATE fx-19 (2026-11-01): the parthian-empire dossier now agrees with this one: its vassal_start for Persis is at -138 (ledger/15), its vassal_end and the loss of the Persis land are at 224 (ledger/65, /64), and its -144 keyframe no longer draws Persis. Pages re-read: Kings of Persis ('Vassal of the Parthian Empire'; 'Incorporated into the Sasanian Empire: AD 224'; Ardashir V last king 211/2-224) and Ardashir I (no year earlier than 224 for Persis leaving Parthian overlordship). Still open, for the sasanian-empire owner: its /ledger/0 found of 215 takes the Persis land (counterpart persis) nine years before the pages' 224.
